finding: PL-1 MED principle api.ts:4326-4340 — agent with review:approve (delegatedReviewer) skips review audience check while the backing human is refused → agent > human power inversion.

commits.subject: Hold a review:approve agent to its human's Review audience
commits.body:
PL-1: at a human Review gate, a caller with a verified human subject must be
in the step's audience, but an undelegated agent with review:approve skipped
that check entirely. The human the agent works for was refused ("assigned to
someone else") while their agent confirmed — an agent holding more power
than its human.

The agent now passes only where the human its task works for (resolved as
for Avatar invocation: the creator chain, an Avatar's owner) would; an agent
with no resolvable human cannot confirm a human gate.

finding: PL-2 MED security api.ts:2206-2287 updateArmedParams doesn't strip _githubAccountId (and _authorization/_forkWorld/_workflowRunId) unlike createTask (api.ts:1108). Quick.

commits.subject: Keep a task's pinned GitHub account through a full-form params edit
commits.body:
A replace edit rebuilds params from the form plus a short list of
platform-owned fields; `_githubAccountId` was not on it. The form cannot
send it (and PL-2 now strips any caller copy), so editing a draft silently
unpinned the account its PRs are opened as, falling back to whichever
account the user has active later.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Never take platform metadata from a draft or armed params edit
commits.body:
PL-2: createTask strips caller-supplied `_authorization`/`_githubAccountId`,
but updateArmedParams merged the caller's params over the stored ones and
only restored `_authorization` when the task already had one. A task:edit
token could therefore substitute the GitHub account a task's PRs are opened
as, point it at another `_workflowRunId`, set one-shot start flags, and — on
a task created before authorization snapshots — write its own
`_authorization: { capabilities: ['*'] }`.

Both paths now drop every `_`-prefixed key a caller sends: those are
platform-written metadata by convention, so one rule covers fields added
later too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

finding: PL-3 MED security api.ts:4940 queueView scopes projectId ?? caller.projectId; multi-project token → unfiltered view leaks other tenants' task ids in same merge domain. Quick.

commits.subject: Filter the merge-queue view by what the token may read
commits.body:
PL-3: queueView filtered only by `projectId ?? caller.projectId`. A token
scoped to a project list or to a whole organization has no single
projectId, so it got the raw queue — every task id in the merge domain,
including other organizations' when they merge into the same repository.

Each queued id is now shown only if the token passes queue:read on that
task's project and organization (and matches a named projectId), so project
lists, organization scopes and deleted tasks are all handled by the one
authorization check instead of a special case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

finding: PL-4 MED security tools.ts:730-742/runtime.ts:146 create_review_info html/links/diff no size cap/validation → Temporal history bloat. Quick.

commits.subject: Bound and validate agent-authored review info
commits.body:
PL-4: create_review_info accepted html, diff, links and actions of any size
and shape and appended actions across calls without limit; every TurnResult
carries the accumulated review info into workflow history, so one agent could
bloat its execution toward Temporal's payload and history limits.

UI-2 (server half): links, `open` targets and `openUrls` are rendered as
clickable URLs in the console, and nothing refused `javascript:`/`data:`.
The handler also passed actions through verbatim, so an agent could mint a
platform-only `payment` approve button under an innocent label.

A new review-info module normalizes each call (run/open actions with only
their own fields, http(s)-only URLs, bounded labels, commands, html and
diff) and the runtime bounds the accumulated total (20 actions, 192 KiB).
Rejections return to the agent as a correctable tool result, as the caption
limit already did.

finding: PL-8 LOW permission-requests.ts single kv blob; in-process dedupe only (multi-replica double apply).

commits.subject: Claim authorization decisions before applying grants
commits.body: Close the AuthorizationRequests analogue of PL-8: persist an owner-bound decision claim before any task or Avatar grant changes, and reject concurrent approvals, denials and dismissals from another gateway. Keep incomplete claims rather than time out a possibly partial side effect. Verify competing API instances and claim persistence across a database restart.

commits.subject: Claim permission-request decisions in the store, not in process memory
commits.body:
PL-8: resolvePermissionRequest kept "decision in progress" in a Set on the
KarmaxApi instance. The request blob itself is safe — every Store
transaction takes the cross-process advisory lock — but an approval that
widens a task's project scope applies setTaskAuthorization before the
request is marked resolved. A denial landing in that window on another
gateway replica (or a rolling-deploy twin) was accepted, and the approval
then failed with "already denied" after the scope had already grown: the
task kept access its approver's peer had just refused.

PermissionRequests.claim/release keep a short-lived claim row in the shared
kv; resolve and dismiss refuse while someone else's claim is live, and a
claim abandoned by a crashed replica expires after five minutes. The API
takes the claim after routing checks and holds it across the side effects;
the post-authorization auto-resolve loop claims too, so it still skips the
request a manual approval is finishing. Task deletion removes claim rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.body:

validated — the API walked only `agent:*` keys — and runAgentTurn loaded the
source task's native session, visible transcript and remote world with no
tenant check at all. Any task:create token could therefore pull another
organization's conversation into a Review agent it controls.

The API validator now walks every agent spec by shape (agent roles, Review
layers including the legacy single gate, the Responder). The activity refuses
a source outside the task's organization, and checks task:conversation:read
on the source with the turn's own minted token, so a pointer that outlived
its creation-time check (spawned runs, older tasks) still cannot widen what
the agent could read through get_conversation.

commits.subject: Trust operator Git configuration; refuse repository transport programs
commits.body:
#369 (RT-5) ran host Git with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and no system
config, which dropped operators' LFS filters, credential helpers and the
environment config chains appendGitConfig extends (it broke the companion
wiki PR test). Only the repository's own configuration is writable from an
agent's checkout, so scan just the local/worktree scopes (includes resolve
to the including scope) and keep an allowlisted operator environment.

The scan also missed programs repository config can run on the host:
remote.<name>.uploadpack/receivepack (executed by a plain fetch from a
local-path remote, verified on git 2.39), core.askPass and
submodule.<name>.update.

commits.body:

answer were archived verbatim in the event log and task view. Key-based
activity redaction only catches `token=…`-shaped text; a DATABASE_URL with
an embedded password, or a bare token, went straight in.

model credential, project/vault secret env including mid-turn refreshes,
secret-looking git env) in a SecretScrubber and replaces them in
agent.output, agent.activity and the returned output. Values under eight
characters are skipped so ordinary text is not mangled.

finding: RT-28 LOW profiles.ts:114 task profiles map unvalidated; can load other org's profile id.

commits.subject: Keep task role profiles inside the task's project and organization
commits.body:
RT-28: a task's `profiles` map (role → profile id) was stored unvalidated
and ProfileResolver loaded whatever id it named. Profile ids are scoped by
prefix (`organization:<org>::…`, `<project>::…`), so a task could name
another tenant's profile and run with its prompt template, model and tool
connections.

profileVisibleTo encodes the scoping rule; the resolver ignores an id
outside the task's project/organization (falling back to the role default),
and createTask/updateArmedParams refuse one with a validation error.
